title: VPC State‑Stream Patcher and Transactional Upgrade Broker for Private Migrations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Upgrading Redwood Private installations in VPC/on‑prem environments requires coordinated schema changes, runtime binary swaps, and kv-store transformations while minimizing downtime for workloads that are latency-sensitive. Current tooling handles orchestration at a coarse level, but customers still report drift during multi-node upgrades, partial rollback complexity, and manual interventions for transactional state reconciliation.

Proposal: Implement a new ‘State‑Stream Patcher’ combined with a ‘Transactional Upgrade Broker’ (TUB). The State‑Stream Patcher consumes a validated stream of preflight diffs (calculated from preflight probes and schema/snapshot comparisons) and applies small idempotent patches to node-local state and cache metadata. The TUB sequences upgrade transactions across cohort nodes, holds a two‑phase commit (2PC)-like token for each upgrade step, and coordinates ephemeral compatibility shims for model runtime and agent handshakes. This approach reduces blast radius by making each step small, observable, and reversible.

Architecture & Components:
- State‑Stream Patcher: lightweight agent that runs next to the existing private agent; applies JSONPath patches, KV rewrite operations, and optionally runs member-level migration hooks. Built with idempotency and backoff.
- Transactional Upgrade Broker: control-plane component in the Private control plane (or local control for air‑gapped installs) that manages cohorts, issues timeboxed tokens, and evaluates programmable rollout gates (health, latency, token errors, regression signals).
- Rollout Gate Integrations: integrates with Console telemetry to use cost/latency regressions, eval set regressions, and SLO error budgets as gate signals (canary failure, alarm threshold, slow token propagation).
- Compatibility Shims: temporary adapters loaded during the transition window to allow old agents to accept new API payload shapes and vice versa. Shims garbage-collect when cohort reports completeness.

Safety & Rollback:
- All patches are versioned and recorded in a per-cohort changelog; TUB keeps a reverse patch that can be applied automatically on failure thresholds.
- Canary semantics: cohort size control, staged intervals, and automated rollback on gate failure.
- Preflight dry-run step that generates a dry-run changelog and a risk score (checks schema diffs, disk availability, network RTT, and KV size).

KMS & Secrets: Patcher will use the host KMS plugin abstraction (existing private KMS integration) for any key material transformations; transformations that touch secrets are only allowed in cohorts with explicit admin approval.

Observability & Telemetry:
- Per-step traces, token lifespan metrics, patch application latencies, and per-node success/failure counters emitted to Console ingestion.
- Dashboard mockup and alert rules: upgrade‑flow latency P95, patch rollback rate, cohort failure rate.

Testing Plan:
- Local simulator for multi-node upgrades (chaos injection: network partition, disk saturation, agent restart).
- Integration tests: run against a cloned private cluster with representative data sizes and a suite of schema/kv transformations.
- Customer beta: 3 selected customers on dedicated capacity, sign-ups gated by support & CSM.

APIs & UX:
- CLI: redwoodctl private upgrade plan/apply --cohort=<ids> --staged-interval=10m --dry-run
- Console: Add an Upgrade Run view with step-level timeline, cohort membership, and one-click rollback.

Artifacts & Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/State+Stream+Patcher+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-upgrades/pull/422
- Telemetry dashboard mock: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/upgrade/patcher-metrics

Open decisions / trade-offs: 
- 2PC vs optimistic sequencing: 2PC provides stronger guarantees but increases coordination traffic and lock durations; current plan uses a tokenized 2PC-lite where tokens expire to avoid indefinite locks.
- Where to run TUB for air‑gapped installs: option A run as a control-plane replica inside the customer VPC (preferred); option B a transient operator run from the customer admin workstation (higher operational burden).
- Backwards compatibility window length: default 7 days but configurable per-release. Longer windows reduce risk but increase maintenance burden for compatibility shims.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End‑to‑end upgrade of a 5‑node private cluster with a complex KV rewrite completes without manual intervention in <= 45 minutes for the staged plan.
- Automatic rollback triggers on gate failures (SLO, latency, or patch errors) and restores nodes to previous state within 10 minutes.
- Telemetry captures 100% of step transitions and exposes cohort membership.

Next steps / Milestones:
- Week 1 (2026-03-15): Finalize design and schema for patch operations; land prototype POC with single-node patcher.
- Week 2 (2026-03-22): Implement TUB baseline and token lifecycle; integrate dry-run generator.
- Week 3 (2026-03-29): Multi-node simulator tests + chaos scenarios.
- Week 4 (2026-04-05): Internal dogfood on infra cluster + initial customer beta outreach.

Notes / Contextual links:
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-33188 (canary migration play), ENG-61234 (incremental-upgrade-catalog).
- Incident learnings: see postmortem for PM-4201 where a mid-upgrade KV rewrite caused partial read failures; lessons applied include preflight size checks and per-patch idempotency.
